o: Estando en esto, comenzó a dar voces don Quijote, diciendo.
t: While this was going on, Don Quixote began to cry out, saying:

o: — Aquí, aquí, valerosos caballeros; aquí es menester mostrar la fuerza de vuestros valerosos brazos, que los cortesanos llevan lo mejor del torneo.
t: "— Here, here, valiant knights; here it is needful to show the strength of your brave arms, for the courtiers carry off the prize of the tournament."

o: Cuando llegaron a don Quijote, ya él estaba levantado de la cama, y proseguía en sus voces y en sus desatinos, dando cuchilladas y reveses a todas partes, estando tan despierto como si nunca hubiera dormido.
t: When they reached Don Quixote, he had already risen from the bed and went on with his cries and his follies, slashing and cutting to all sides, as wide awake as if he had never slept.

o: Abrazáronse con él, y por fuerza le volvieron al lecho; y, después que hubo sosegado un poco, volviéndose a hablar con el cura, le dijo.
t: They embraced him and forcibly took him back to bed; and after he had calmed down a little, turning to speak with the priest, he said:

o: — Por cierto, señor arzobispo Turpín, que es gran mengua de los que nos llamamos doce Pares dejar, tan sin más ni más, llevar la vitoria deste torneo a los caballeros cortesanos, habiendo nosotros los aventureros ganado el prez en los tres días antecedentes.
t: — By the way, Archbishop Turpin, who is a great glutton, one of us who call ourselves the Twelve Peers, just let the courtly knights carry off the victory of this tournament, when we adventurers have won the prize in the three days past.

o: — Calle vuestra merced, señor compadre —dijo el cura—, que Dios será servido que la suerte se mude, y que lo que hoy se pierde se gane mañana; y atienda vuestra merced a su salud por agora, que me parece que debe de estar demasiadamente cansado, si ya no es que está malferido.
t: — Quiet, your worship, sir godfather —said the curate—, for God will be pleased that the luck should turn, and what is lost today be won tomorrow; and let your worship look after his health for now, for it seems to me he must be excessively tired, unless he is badly wounded.

o: — Ferido no —dijo don Quijote—, pero molido y quebrantado, no hay duda en ello; porque aquel bastardo de don Roldán me ha molido a palos con el tronco de una encina, y todo de envidia, porque ve que yo solo soy el opuesto de sus valentías.
t: — Not wounded —said Don Quixote—, but beaten and battered, there's no doubt of it; because that bastard of Don Roldán has beaten me with cudgels, with the trunk of an oak, and all out of envy, because he sees that I alone am the opposite of his valor.

o: Mas no me llamaría yo Reinaldos de Montalbán si, en levantándome deste lecho, no me lo pagare, a pesar de todos sus encantamentos; y, por agora, tráiganme de yantar, que sé que es lo que más me hará al caso, y quédese lo del vengarme a mi cargo.
t: But I should not call myself Rinaldo of Montalban if, when I rise from this bed, I do not pay him back, in spite of all his enchantments; and for now, bring me something to eat, for I know that is what will serve me best, and leave the matter of my revenge to me.

o: Hiciéronlo ansí: diéronle de comer, y quedóse otra vez dormido, y ellos, admirados de su locura.
t: They did so: they gave him to eat, and he fell asleep again, and they, amazed at his madness.

o: Aquella noche quemó y abrasó el ama cuantos libros había en el corral y en toda la casa, y tales debieron de arder que merecían guardarse en perpetuos archivos; mas no lo permitió su suerte y la pereza del escrutiñador; y así, se cumplió el refrán en ellos de que pagan a las veces justos por pecadores.
t: That night the housekeeper burned and singed as many books as there were in the yard and in the whole house, and such must have been the ones that burned that they deserved to be kept in perpetual archives; but his luck and the laziness of the scrivener did not permit it; and so the proverb was fulfilled in them, that at times the just pay for the sinners.

o: Uno de los remedios que el cura y el barbero dieron, por entonces, para el mal de su amigo, fue que le murasen y tapiasen el aposento de los libros, porque cuando se levantase no los hallase —quizá quitando la causa, cesaría el efeto—, y que dijesen que un encantador se los había llevado, y el aposento y todo; y así fue hecho con mucha presteza.
t: One of the remedies the curate and the barber gave, for the time being, for their friend's ailment, was that they walled up and plastered over the room of the books, so that when he got up he would not find them —perhaps removing the cause, the effect would cease—, and that they should say a sorcerer had carried them off, the room and all; and so it was done with great haste.

o: De allí a dos días se levantó don Quijote, y lo primero que hizo fue ir a.
t: Two days later Don Quixote got up, and the first thing he did was to go and

o: ver sus libros; y, como no hallaba el aposento donde le había dejado, andaba de una en otra parte buscándole.
t: see his books; and, since he did not find the room where he had left them, he went about from one place to another looking for it.

o: Llegaba adonde solía tener la puerta, y tentábala con las manos, y volvía y revolvía los ojos por todo, sin decir palabra; pero, al cabo de una buena pieza, preguntó a su ama que hacia qué parte estaba el aposento de sus libros.
t: He came to where the door used to be, and tried it with his hands, and turned and rolled his eyes about everywhere, without saying a word; but, after a good while, he asked his housekeeper which way the room of his books was.

o: El ama, que ya estaba bien advertida de lo que había de responder, le dijo.
t: The housekeeper, who had already been well instructed in what she was to answer, told him.

o: — ¿Qué aposento, o qué nada, busca vuestra merced?
t: — What room, or what anything at all, is your worship looking for?

o: Ya no hay aposento ni libros en esta casa, porque todo se lo llevó el mesmo diablo.
t: There is no room nor books in this house any longer, because the very devil took them all away.

o: Dijo también que se llamaba el sabio Muñatón.
t: She also said that the wise Muñatón was the name.

o: — Frestón diría —dijo don Quijote.
t: — Frestón, I should say —said Don Quixote.

o: — No sé —respondió el ama— si se llamaba Frestón o Fritón; sólo sé que acabó en tón su nombre.
t: — I don't know —answered the housekeeper— whether it was called Frestón or Fritón; I only know that his name ended in -tón.

o: — ¿Quién duda de eso?
t: — Who doubts that?

o: —dijo la sobrina—.
t: —said the niece—.

o: Pero, ¿quién le mete a vuestra merced, señor tío, en esas pendencias?
t: But, who is putting your worship, uncle sir, into such troubles?

o: ¿No será mejor estarse pacífico en su casa y no irse por el mundo a buscar pan de trastrigo, sin considerar que muchos van por lana y vuelven tresquilados?
t: Would it not be better to stay quietly at home and not go roaming the world seeking bread of trashy wheat, without considering that many go for wool and come back shorn?

o: — ¡Oh sobrina mía —respondió don Quijote—, y cuán mal que estás en la cuenta!
t: "Oh, my niece," replied Don Quixote, "and how badly you keep the tally!"

o: Primero que a mí me tresquilen, tendré peladas y quitadas las barbas a cuantos imaginaren tocarme en la punta de un solo cabello.
t: Before anyone lays a hand on me, I shall have shaved and plucked the beards of all who so much as dream of touching me at the tip of a single hair.

o: No quisieron las dos replicarle más, porque vieron que se le encendía la cólera.
t: The two of them did not try to answer him further, for they saw that his anger was flaring.

o: El cura algunas veces le contradecía y otras concedía, porque si no guardaba este artificio, no había poder averiguarse con él.
t: The curate sometimes contradicted him and sometimes conceded, because if he did not resort to this device, there was no way of getting to the bottom of him.

o: En este tiempo, solicitó don Quijote a un labrador vecino suyo, hombre de bien —si es que este título se puede dar al que es pobre—, pero de muy poca sal en la mollera.
t: Meanwhile, Don Quixote asked a neighboring farmer, a good man —if that title can be given to one who is poor— but of very little wit in his head.

o: En resolución, tanto le dijo, tanto le persuadió y prometió, que el pobre villano se determinó de salirse con él y servirle de escudero.
t: In short, he talked and persuaded and promised so much that the poor rustic made up his mind to go off with him and serve him as squire.

o: Decíale, entre otras cosas, don Quijote que se dispusiese a ir con él de buena gana, porque tal vez le podía suceder aventura que ganase, en quítame allá esas pajas, alguna ínsula, y le dejase a él por gobernador della.
t: Among other things, Don Quixote told him to make ready to go with him willingly, because perhaps some adventure might befall him in which he might win, "remove that straw from my teeth," some island, and leave him governor of it.

o: Con estas promesas y otras tales, Sancho Panza, que así se llamaba el labrador, dejó su mujer y hijos y asentó por escudero de su vecino.
t: With these and other such promises, Sancho Panza — for so the farmer was called — left his wife and children and settled in as his neighbor's squire.

o: Dio luego don Quijote orden en buscar dineros; y, vendiendo una cosa y empeñando otra, y malbaratándolas todas, llegó una razonable cantidad.
t: Don Quixote then gave orders to look for money; and by selling one thing and pawning another, and squandering them all, he managed to gather a reasonable sum.

o: Acomodóse asimesmo de una rodela, que pidió prestada a un su amigo, y, pertrechando su rota celada lo mejor que pudo, avisó a su escudero Sancho del día y la hora que pensaba ponerse en camino, para que él se acomodase de lo que viese que más le era menester.
t: He fitted himself out with a buckler, which he borrowed from a friend, and, patching up his battered helmet as best he could, he let his squire Sancho know the day and hour he meant to set out, so that he might provide himself with whatever he saw fit.

o: Sobre todo le encargó que llevase alforjas; e dijo que sí llevaría, y que ansimesmo pensaba llevar un asno que tenía muy bueno, porque él no estaba duecho a andar mucho a pie.
t: Above all, he charged him to bring saddlebags; and Sancho said he would bring them, and that he meant to bring the ass he had, a very fine one, because he was not used to walking far on foot.

o: Iba Sancho Panza sobre su jumento como un patriarca, con sus alforjas y su bota, y con mucho deseo de verse ya gobernador de la ínsula que su amo le había prometido.
t: Sancho Panza rode his donkey like a patriarch, with his saddlebags and his wineskin, and with a great desire to see himself already governor of the island his master had promised him.

o: Acertó don Quijote a tomar la misma derrota y camino que el que él había tomado en su primer viaje, que fue por el campo de Montiel, por el cual caminaba con menos pesadumbre que la vez pasada, porque, por ser la hora de la mañana y herirles a soslayo los rayos del sol, no les fatigaban.
t: Don Quixote happened to take the same route and road he had taken on his first journey, which was through the field of Montiel, along which he rode with less heaviness than the previous time, because, it being morning and the sun's rays striking them slantingly, they were not tired by them.

o: Dijo en esto Sancho Panza a su amo.
t: Here Sancho Panza said to his master.

o: — Mire vuestra merced, señor caballero andante, que no se le olvide lo que de la ínsula me tiene prometido; que yo la sabré gobernar, por grande que sea.
t: "Look here, your grace, sir knight-errant, don't let what you've promised me about the island slip your mind; for I shall know how to govern it, however great it may be."

o: A lo cual le respondió don Quijote.
t: To which Don Quixote replied.

o: Y no lo tengas a mucho, que cosas y casos acontecen a los tales caballeros, por modos tan nunca vistos ni pensados, que con facilidad te podría dar aún más de lo que te prometo.
t: And don't take it so hard, for things and events befall such knights in ways so far never seen nor imagined that I could easily give you even more than I have promised you.

o: — De esa manera —respondió Sancho Panza—, si yo fuese rey por algún milagro de los que vuestra merced dice, por lo menos, Juana Gutiérrez, mi oíslo, vendría a ser reina, y mis hijos infantes.
t: "In that case," answered Sancho Panza, "if by some miracle of the kind your grace mentions I were king, then at least Juana Gutiérrez, my wife, would be queen, and my children would be infants."

o: — Pues, ¿quién lo duda?
t: "Well, who doubts it?"

o: —respondió don Quijote.
t: "replied Don Quixote.

o: — Yo lo dudo —replicó Sancho Panza—; porque tengo para mí que, aunque lloviese Dios reinos sobre la tierra, ninguno asentaría bien sobre la cabeza de Mari Gutiérrez.
t: "I doubt it," replied Sancho Panza, "for I have it for certain that, even if God should rain kingdoms down on the earth, none of them would sit well on the head of Mari Gutiérrez."

o: Sepa, señor, que no vale dos maravedís para reina; condesa le caerá mejor, y aun Dios y ayuda.
t: "Know, sir, that she is not worth two maravedís as a queen; a countess will suit her better, and God and good luck go with her."

o: — Encomiéndalo tú a Dios, Sancho —respondió don Quijote—, que Él dará lo que más le convenga, pero no apoques tu ánimo tanto, que te vengas a contentar con menos que con ser adelantado.
t: "Commend her to God, Sancho," replied Don Quixote; "He will give her what is best for her, but do not let your spirit sink so low that you come to be content with less than being a squire."

o: — No lo haré, señor mío —respondió Sancho—; y más teniendo tan principal amo en vuestra merced, que me sabrá dar todo aquello que me esté bien y yo pueda llevar.
t: "I will not do so, my lord," replied Sancho; "especially having so noble a master in your grace, who will know how to give me everything that suits me and that I can carry."

o: Del buen suceso que el valeroso don Quijote tuvo en la espantable y jamás imaginada aventura de los molinos de viento, con otros sucesos dignos de felice recordación.
t: Of the good success that the valiant Don Quixote had in the dread and never-imagined adventure of the windmills, with other events worthy of happy remembrance.

o: En esto, descubrieron treinta o cuarenta molinos de viento que hay en aquel campo; y, así como don Quijote los vio, dijo a su escudero.
t: In the course of this they came upon thirty or forty windmills that stand in that field; and as soon as Don Quixote saw them, he said to his squire.

o: —dijo Sancho Panza.
t: "—said Sancho Panza."

o: — Aquellos que allí ves —respondió su amo— de los brazos largos, que los suelen tener algunos de casi dos leguas.
t: "Those you see over there," replied his master, "with the long arms; some of them are nearly two leagues long."

o: — Mire vuestra merced —respondió Sancho— que aquellos que allí se parecen no son gigantes, sino molinos de viento, y lo que en ellos parecen brazos son las aspas, que, volteadas del viento, hacen andar la piedra del molino.
t: "Look at your grace," replied Sancho, "those things that look like men there are not giants, but windmills; and what seem to be arms are the sails, which, turned by the wind, set the millstone going."

o: — Bien parece —respondió don Quijote— que no estás cursado en esto de las aventuras: ellos son gigantes; y si tienes miedo, quítate de ahí, y ponte en oración en el espacio que yo voy a entrar con ellos en fiera y desigual batalla.
t: "It seems plain enough," replied Don Quixote, "that you are not used to this business of adventures: they are giants; and if you are afraid, get out of the way and set yourself to prayer while I go into fierce and unequal battle with them."

o: Y, diciendo esto, dio de espuelas a su caballo Rocinante, sin atender a las voces que su escudero Sancho le daba, advirtiéndole que, sin duda alguna, eran molinos de viento, y no gigantes, aquellos que iba a acometer.
t: Saying this, he spurred his horse Rocinante, without heeding the cries his squire Sancho was giving him, warning him that beyond any doubt those he was going to attack were windmills and not giants.

o: Pero él iba tan puesto en que eran gigantes, que ni oía las voces de su escudero Sancho ni echaba de ver, aunque estaba ya bien cerca, lo que eran; antes, iba diciendo en voces altas.
t: But he was so convinced they were giants that he neither heard his squire Sancho's voice nor noticed, though he was already close by, what they truly were; on the contrary, he went on saying aloud:

o: — Non fuyades, cobardes y viles criaturas, que un solo caballero es el que os acomete.
t: "Fly not, cowardly and vile creatures, for a single knight is he who attacks you."

o: Levantóse en esto un poco de viento y las grandes aspas comenzaron a moverse, lo cual visto por don Quijote, dijo.
t: Thereupon a little wind rose and the great sails began to move, which Don Quixote, seeing, said:

o: — Pues, aunque mováis más brazos que los del gigante Briareo, me lo habéis de pagar.
t: "Well, though you move more arms than the giant Briareus, you shall pay me for it."

o: Acudió Sancho Panza a socorrerle, a todo el correr de su asno, y cuando llegó halló que no se podía menear: tal fue el golpe que dio con él Rocinante.
t: Sancho Panza came to his aid, at the full gallop of his donkey, and when he arrived he found that Don Quixote could not stir: such was the blow that Rocinante had dealt him.

o: ¿No le dije yo a vuestra merced que mirase bien lo que hacía, que no eran sino molinos de viento, y no lo podía ignorar sino quien llevase otros tales en la cabeza?
t: "Did I not tell your grace to look well at what you were doing, that they were nothing but windmills, and that only one who had such things in his head could fail to see it?"

o: — Dios lo haga como puede —respondió Sancho Panza.
t: "God make of it as He can," replied Sancho Panza.

o: Y, ayudándole a levantar, tornó a subir sobre Rocinante, que medio despaldado estaba.
t: And, helping him to get up, he mounted Rocinante again, though the horse was half foundered.

o: Y, hablando en la pasada aventura, siguieron el camino del Puerto Lápice, porque allí decía don Quijote que no era posible dejar de hallarse muchas y diversas aventuras, por ser lugar muy pasajero; sino que iba muy pesaroso por haberle faltado la lanza; y, diciéndoselo a su escudero, le dijo.
t: And, speaking of the previous adventure, they followed the road to Puerto Lápice, because there Don Quixote said it was impossible not to encounter many and diverse adventures, since it was a very busy place; but he was going very sorrowful, for having lost his lance; and, telling this to his squire, he said to him.

o: Hete dicho esto, porque de la primera encina o roble que se me depare pienso desgajar otro tronco tal y tan bueno como aquél, que me imagino y pienso hacer con él tales hazañas, que tú te tengas por bien afortunado de haber merecido venir a vellas y a ser testigo de cosas que apenas podrán ser creídas.
t: I have told you this, because from the first oak or holly tree that comes my way I mean to break off another branch, as good and as stout as that one, with which I imagine and intend to perform such deeds that you should count yourself lucky to have deserved to come with me and to be a witness of things that will scarcely be believed.

o: — A la mano de Dios —dijo Sancho—; yo lo creo todo así como vuestra merced lo dice; pero enderécese un poco, que parece que va de medio lado, y debe de ser del molimiento de la caída.
t: "God's will be done," said Sancho; "I believe it all just as your grace says; but straighten yourself a little, for you seem to be going half sideways, and it must be from the bruising of the fall."

o: — Así es la verdad —respondió don Quijote—; y si no me quejo del dolor, es porque no es dado a los caballeros andantes quejarse de herida alguna, aunque se le salgan las tripas por ella.
t: "That is the truth," replied Don Quixote; "and if I do not complain of the pain, it is because it is not fitting for knights-errant to complain of any wound, even if their guts spill out through it."

o: — Si eso es así, no tengo yo qué replicar —respondió Sancho—, pero sabe Dios si yo me holgara que vuestra merced se quejara cuando alguna cosa le doliera.
t: "If that is so, I have nothing to answer," replied Sancho; "but God knows whether I would rejoice if your grace would complain whenever something hurt you."

o: De mí sé decir que me he de quejar del más pequeño dolor que tenga, si ya no se entiende también con los escuderos de los caballeros andantes eso del no quejarse.
t: Of myself I can say that I shall complain of the smallest pain I feel, if the rule that knights-errant do not complain is not also understood to extend to the squires of knights-errant.

o: No se dejó de reír don Quijote de la simplicidad de su escudero; y así, le declaró que podía muy bien quejarse, como y cuando quisiese, sin gana o con ella; que hasta entonces no había leído cosa en contrario en la orden de caballería.
t: Don Quixote could not help laughing at the simplicity of his squire; and so he declared to him that he might very well complain, whenever and however he wished, whether he felt like it or not; for until then he had read nothing to the contrary in the order of chivalry.

o: Díjole Sancho que mirase que era hora de comer.
t: Sancho told him it was time to eat.

o: Respondióle su amo que por entonces no le hacía menester; que comiese él cuando se le antojase.
t: His master replied that for the moment he had no need of it; that he should eat whenever he pleased.

o: Con esta licencia, se acomodó Sancho lo mejor que pudo sobre su jumento, y, sacando de las alforjas lo que en ellas había puesto, iba caminando y comiendo detrás de su amo muy de su espacio, y de cuando en cuando empinaba la bota, con tanto gusto, que le pudiera envidiar el más regalado bodegonero de Málaga.
t: With this permission, Sancho settled himself as comfortably as he could on his donkey, and, taking out of the saddlebags what he had put in them, he went along walking and eating behind his master very leisurely, and from time to time he tilted the boot up, with such relish that the most pampered tavernkeeper of Málaga might have envied him.

o: Y, en tanto que él iba de aquella manera menudeando tragos, no se le acordaba de ninguna promesa que su amo le hubiese hecho, ni tenía por ningún trabajo, sino por mucho descanso, andar buscando las aventuras, por peligrosas que fuesen.
t: And while he went on in that manner, sipping little and often, he remembered none of the promises his master had made him, nor did he trouble himself at all, but only took great ease and pleasure in seeking out adventures, however dangerous they might be.

o: En resolución, aquella noche la pasaron entre unos árboles, y del uno dellos desgajó don Quijote un ramo seco que casi le podía servir de lanza, y puso en él el hierro que quitó de la que se le había quebrado.
t: In short, they spent that night among some trees, and from one of them Don Quixote broke off a dry branch that could almost serve him as a lance, and he fitted it with the iron head he had taken from the one that had broken.

o: Toda aquella noche no durmió don Quijote, pensando en su señora Dulcinea, por acomodarse a lo que había leído en sus libros, cuando los caballeros pasaban sin dormir muchas noches en las florestas y despoblados, entretenidos con las memorias de sus señoras.
t: All that night Don Quixote did not sleep, thinking of his lady Dulcinea, to conform to what he had read in his books, how knights passed many sleepless nights in forests and wildernesses, keeping themselves occupied with the memories of their ladies.

o: No la pasó ansí Sancho Panza, que, como tenía el estómago lleno, y no de agua de chicoria, de un sueño se la llevó toda; y no fueran parte para despertarle, si su amo no lo llamara, los rayos del sol, que le daban en el rostro, ni el canto de las aves, que, muchas y muy regocijadamente, la venida del nuevo día saludaban.
t: Sancho Panza did not pass the night so, for, his stomach being full—not of chicory water but of good fare—a single sleep took him all in; and neither the rays of the sun, which struck him in the face, nor the song of the birds, which in great numbers and with great rejoicing were welcoming the coming of the new day, would have been able to wake him, had not his master called him.

o: Al levantarse dio un tiento a la bota, y hallóla algo más flaca que la noche antes; y afligiósele el corazón, por parecerle que no llevaban camino de remediar tan presto su falta.
t: On rising he felt for his wineskin, and found it a little emptier than the night before; and his heart was afflicted, for it seemed to him that they were not on the way to so soon make good his lack.

o: No quiso desayunarse don Quijote, porque, como está dicho, dio en sustentarse de sabrosas memorias.
t: Don Quixote did not care to break his fast, for, as has been said, he began to sustain himself on savoury memories.

o: Tornaron a su comenzado camino del Puerto Lápice, y a obra de las tres del día le descubrieron.
t: They returned to the road they had started upon, that of the Pass of Lápice, and at about three o'clock in the day they came in sight of it.

o: — Aquí —dijo, en viéndole, don Quijote— podemos, hermano Sancho Panza, meter las manos hasta los codos en esto que llaman aventuras.
t: "Here," said Don Quixote, when he saw it, "we can, brother Sancho Panza, thrust our hands up to the elbows into what they call adventures."

o: — Por cierto, señor —respondió Sancho—, que vuestra merced sea muy bien obedicido en esto; y más, que yo de mío me soy pacífico y enemigo de meterme en ruidos ni pendencias.
t: "Indeed, sir," answered Sancho, "your worship will be very well obeyed in this; and moreover, of my own accord I am peaceful and an enemy of getting myself into quarrels and bickerings."

o: Bien es verdad que, en lo que tocare a defender mi persona, no tendré mucha cuenta con esas leyes, pues las divinas y humanas permiten que cada uno se defienda de quien quisiere agraviarle.
t: It is true that, as concerns the defence of my own person, I shall not pay much heed to those laws, since the divine and human laws permit each man to defend himself against whoever wishes to do him harm.

o: — No digo yo menos —respondió don Quijote—; pero, en esto de ayudarme contra caballeros, has de tener a raya tus naturales ímpetus.
t: "I'm not saying otherwise," replied Don Quixote, "but as for helping me against knights, you must keep your natural impetuses within bounds."

o: — Digo que así lo haré —respondió Sancho—, y que guardaré ese preceto tan bien como el día del domingo.
t: "I say I will do so," replied Sancho, "and I'll keep that precept as well as I keep Sunday."

o: Estando en estas razones, asomaron por el camino dos frailes de la orden de San Benito, caballeros sobre dos dromedarios: que no eran más pequeñas dos mulas en que venían.
t: While they were talking, two friars of the Order of Saint Benedict appeared on the road, mounted on two dromedaries: they were no smaller than the two mules they rode.

o: Traían sus antojos de camino y sus quitasoles.
t: They carried their traveling provisions and their sunshades.

o: Detrás dellos venía un coche, con cuatro o cinco de a caballo que le acompañaban y dos mozos de mulas a pie.
t: Behind them came a coach, with four or five horsemen accompanying it and two muleteers on foot.

o: Venía en el coche, como después se supo, una señora vizcaína, que iba a Sevilla, donde estaba su marido, que pasaba a las Indias con un muy honroso cargo.
t: In the coach, as was learned later, was a Basque lady on her way to Seville, where her husband was, who was passing on to the Indies with a very honorable post.

o: No venían los frailes con ella, aunque iban el mesmo camino; mas, apenas los divisó don Quijote, cuando dijo a su escudero.
t: The friars were not traveling with her, though they were on the same road; but as soon as Don Quixote spied them, he said to his squire.

o: — O yo me engaño, o ésta ha de ser la más famosa aventura que se haya visto; porque aquellos bultos negros que allí parecen deben de ser, y son sin duda, algunos encantadores que llevan hurtada alguna princesa en aquel coche, y es menester deshacer este tuerto a todo mi poderío.
t: "Either I am mistaken, or this must be the most famous adventure ever seen; for those black shapes over there must be, and are undoubtedly, some enchanters who have carried off some princess in that coach, and it is necessary to undo this wrong with all my might."

o: — Peor será esto que los molinos de viento —dijo Sancho—.
t: "This will be worse than the windmills," said Sancho.

o: Mire, señor, que aquéllos son frailes de San Benito, y el coche debe de ser de alguna gente pasajera.
t: "Look, sir, those are friars of Saint Benedict, and the coach must belong to some ordinary travelers."

o: Mire que digo que mire bien lo que hace, no sea el diablo que le engañe.
t: "See what I mean, see well what you are doing; don't let the devil deceive you."

o: — Ya te he dicho, Sancho —respondió don Quijote—, que sabes poco de achaque de aventuras; lo que yo digo es verdad, y ahora lo verás.
t: "I have already told you, Sancho," replied Don Quixote, "that you know little about the matter of adventures; what I say is the truth, and now you will see it."

o: Y, diciendo esto, se adelantó y se puso en la mitad del camino por donde los frailes venían, y, en llegando tan cerca que a él le pareció que le podrían oír lo que dijese, en alta voz dijo.
t: Saying this, he rode forward and placed himself in the middle of the road by which the friars were coming, and, when he was close enough for them to hear what he said, he spoke in a loud voice.

o: — Gente endiablada y descomunal, dejad luego al punto las altas princesas que en ese coche lleváis forzadas; si no, aparejaos a recebir presta muerte, por justo castigo de vuestras malas obras.
t: "Devilish and monstrous people, immediately release the noble princesses you are carrying by force in that coach; otherwise, prepare to receive a swift death, as just punishment for your evil deeds."

o: Detuvieron los frailes las riendas, y quedaron admirados, así de la figura de don Quijote como de sus razones, a las cuales respondieron.
t: The friars reined in their mounts and were astounded, both at Don Quixote's appearance and at his words, to which they replied.

o: — Señor caballero, nosotros no somos endiablados ni descomunales, sino dos religiosos de San Benito que vamos nuestro camino, y no sabemos si en este coche vienen, o no, ningunas forzadas princesas.
t: "Sir knight, we are neither devilish nor monstrous, but two religious of Saint Benedict going our own way, and we know not whether any princesses are being carried by force in that coach or not."

o: — Para conmigo no hay palabras blandas, que ya yo os conozco, fementida canalla —dijo don Quijote.
t: "Soft words are of no avail with me, for I know you well, you foul rabble," said Don Quixote.

o: Y, sin esperar más respuesta, picó a Rocinante y, la lanza baja, arremetió contra el primero fraile, con tanta furia y denuedo que, si el fraile no se dejara caer de la mula, él le hiciera venir al suelo mal de su grado, y aun malferido, si no cayera muerto.
t: And without waiting for further reply, he spurred Rocinante and, lance lowered, charged the first frial, with such fury and boldness that, had the friar not thrown himself from his mule, he would have dragged him to the ground against his will, and badly wounded besides, had he not fallen dead.

o: El segundo religioso, que vio del modo que trataban a su compañero, puso piernas al castillo de su buena mula, y comenzó a correr por aquella campaña, más ligero que el mesmo viento.
t: The second religious, seeing how his companion was being treated, put legs to the stirrups of his good mule and began to run across that plain, lighter than the wind itself.

o: Sancho Panza, que vio en el suelo al fraile, apeándose ligeramente de su asno, arremetió a él y le comenzó a quitar los hábitos.
t: Sancho Panza, who saw the friar on the ground, lightly dismounting from his donkey, charged at him and began to pull off his habit.

o: Llegaron en esto dos mozos de los frailes y preguntáronle que por qué le desnudaba.
t: Two lads from the friars arrived here and asked him why he was stripping him.

o: Respondióles Sancho que aquello le tocaba a él ligítimamente, como despojos de la batalla que su señor don Quijote había ganado.
t: Sancho answered them that it belonged to him legitimately, as spoils of the battle his master Don Quixote had won.

o: Los mozos, que no sabían de burlas, ni entendían aquello de despojos ni batallas, viendo que ya don Quijote estaba desviado de allí, hablando con las que en el coche venían, arremetieron con Sancho y dieron con él en el suelo; y, sin dejarle pelo en las barbas, le molieron a coces y le dejaron tendido en el suelo sin aliento ni sentido.
t: The lads, who knew nothing of jests nor understood anything about spoils or battles, seeing that Don Quixote had already gone off from there, talking with the women who were in the coach, set upon Sancho and knocked him to the ground; and without leaving him a hair of his beard, they beat him to a pulp with kicks and left him stretched on the ground, breathless and senseless.

o: Don Quijote estaba, como se ha dicho, hablando con la señora del coche, diciéndole.
t: Don Quixote was, as has been said, talking with the lady of the coach, telling her.

o: Todo esto que don Quijote decía escuchaba un escudero de los que el coche acompañaban, que era vizcaíno; el cual, viendo que no quería dejar pasar el coche adelante, sino que decía que luego había de dar la vuelta al Toboso, se fue para don Quijote y, asiéndole de la lanza, le dijo, en mala lengua castellana y peor vizcaína, desta manera.
t: All that Don Quixote was saying was overheard by one of the squires who accompanied the coach, a Basque; who, seeing that he would not let the coach go on but said he would presently turn back for the Toboso, went up to Don Quixote and, seizing him by the lance, said to him, in bad Castilian and worse Basque, in this manner.

o: — Anda, caballero que mal andes; por el Dios que crióme, que, si no dejas coche, así te matas como estás ahí vizcaíno.
t: "Come now, knight, you who fare so ill; by the God who made me, if you do not leave the coach, I will kill you as surely as you stand there, Basque."

o: Entendióle muy bien don Quijote, y con mucho sosiego le respondió.
t: Don Quixote understood him very well, and with great composure he replied.

o: — Si fueras caballero, como no lo eres, ya yo hubiera castigado tu sandez y atrevimiento, cautiva criatura.
t: "If you were a knight, as you are not, I would already have punished your folly and your boldness, captive creature."

o: A lo cual replicó el vizcaíno.
t: To which the Basque replied.

o: — ¿Yo no caballero?
t: "Me not a knight?"

o: Juro a Dios tan mientes como cristiano.
t: I swear to God you lie as much as any Christian.

o: Si lanza arrojas y espada sacas, ¡el agua cuán presto verás que al gato llevas!
t: If you throw your lance and draw your sword, you will soon see the water carry your cat away!

o: Vizcaíno por tierra, hidalgo por mar, hidalgo por el diablo; y mientes que mira si otra dices cosa.
t: Basque on land, hidalgo at sea, hidalgo for the devil; and you lie, so tell me if you can say anything else.

o: — ¡Ahora lo veredes, dijo Agrajes!
t: "Now you shall see!" said Agrajes.

o: —respondió don Quijote.
t: "replied Don Quixote.

o: Y, arrojando la lanza en el suelo, sacó su espada y embrazó su rodela, y arremetió al vizcaíno con determinación de quitarle la vida.
t: And, casting his lance on the ground, he drew his sword and set his buckler on his arm, and charged the Basque with the determination to take his life.

o: La demás gente quisiera ponerlos en paz, mas no pudo, porque decía el vizcaíno en sus mal trabadas razones que si no le dejaban acabar su batalla, que él mismo había de matar a su ama y a toda la gente que se lo estorbase.
t: The rest of the people would have set them at peace, but they could not, because the Basque kept saying, in his ill-woven reasons, that if they did not let him finish his battle, he would himself kill his lady and all the people who stood in his way.

o: La señora del coche, admirada y temerosa de lo que veía, hizo al cochero que se desviase de allí algún poco, y desde lejos se puso a mirar la rigurosa contienda, en el discurso de la cual dio el vizcaíno una gran cuchillada a don Quijote encima de un hombro, por encima de la rodela, que, a dársela sin defensa, le abriera hasta la cintura.
t: The lady of the coach, astonished and frightened by what she saw, told the coachman to turn aside a little, and from a distance she began to watch the fierce contest, during which the Basque gave Don Quixote a great slash across the shoulder, over the buckler, which, had it landed without defense, would have cut him to the waist.

o: Don Quijote, que sintió la pesadumbre de aquel desaforado golpe, dio una gran voz, diciendo.
t: Don Quixote, who felt the weight of that unbridled blow, gave a great cry, saying.

o: — ¡Oh señora de mi alma, Dulcinea, flor de la fermosura, socorred a este vuestro caballero, que, por satisfacer a la vuestra mucha bondad, en este riguroso trance se halla!
t: "Oh lady of my soul, Dulcinea, flower of beauty, help this knight of yours, who, to satisfy your great goodness, finds himself in this rigorous strait!"

o: El decir esto, y el apretar la espada, y el cubrirse bien de su rodela, y el arremeter al vizcaíno, todo fue en un tiempo, llevando determinación de aventurarlo todo a la de un golpe solo.
t: Saying this, and gripping his sword, and covering himself well with his buckler, and charging the Basque, all were done at once, with the resolve to risk everything on a single blow.

o: El vizcaíno, que así le vio venir contra él, bien entendió por su denuedo su coraje, y determinó de hacer lo mesmo que don Quijote; y así, le aguardó bien cubierto de su almohada, sin poder rodear la mula a una ni a otra parte; que ya, de puro cansada y no hecha a semejantes niñerías, no podía dar un paso.
t: The Biscayan, seeing him coming at him in this manner, understood from his boldness his courage, and resolved to do the same as Don Quixote; and so he waited for him well covered by his pillow, unable to get around the mule on either side, for she, so worn out and not used to such childish tricks, could not take a step.

o: Pero está el daño de todo esto que en este punto y término deja pendiente el autor desta historia esta batalla, disculpándose que no halló más escrito destas hazañas de don Quijote de las que deja referidas.
t: But here is the harm in all of this: at this point and juncture the author of this history leaves the battle pending, excusing himself that he found nothing more written of the deeds of Don Quixote than what he has already recounted.

o: Segunda parte del ingenioso hidalgo don Quijote de la Mancha.
t: Second part of the ingenious gentleman Don Quixote of La Mancha.

o: Donde se concluye y da fin a la estupenda batalla que el gallardo vizcaíno y el valiente manchego tuvieron.
t: Wherein the stupendous battle between the gallant Biscayan and the valiant Manchegan is concluded and brought to an end.

o: Causóme esto mucha pesadumbre, porque el gusto de haber leído tan poco se volvía en disgusto, de pensar el mal camino que se ofrecía para hallar lo mucho que, a mi parecer, faltaba de tan sabroso cuento.
t: This caused me much distress, because the pleasure of having read so little turned into disappointment at the thought of the bad path that offered itself for finding the abundance that, in my judgment, was lacking in so savory a tale.

o: Parecióme cosa imposible y fuera de toda buena costumbre que a tan buen caballero le hubiese faltado algún sabio que tomara a cargo el escrebir sus nunca vistas hazañas, cosa que no faltó a ninguno de los caballeros andantes.
t: It seemed to me impossible and outside all good custom that such a good gentleman should have lacked some learned man to take charge of writing his never-before-seen deeds, a thing that was not lacking to any of the knights-errant.

o: de los que dicen las gentes que van a sus aventuras.
t: of those whom people say go on their adventures.

o: porque cada uno dellos tenía uno o dos sabios, como de molde, que no solamente escribían sus hechos, sino que pintaban sus más mínimos pensamientos y niñerías, por más escondidas que fuesen; y no había de ser tan desdichado tan buen caballero, que le faltase a él lo que sobró a Platir y a otros semejantes.
t: because each of them had one or two learned men, as a matter of course, who not only wrote down their deeds but also painted their most minute thoughts and trifles, however hidden they might be; and no such good gentleman should be so unfortunate as to lack what was more than enough for Plato and others like him.

o: Y así, no podía inclinarme a creer que tan gallarda historia hubiese quedado manca y estropeada; y echaba la culpa a la malignidad del tiempo, devorador y consumidor de todas las cosas, el cual, o la tenía oculta o consumida.
t: And so I could not bring myself to believe that so gallant a history should have been left limping and mangled; and I blamed the malice of time, the devourer and consumer of all things, which either had hidden it or consumed it.

o: Por otra parte, me parecía que, pues entre sus libros se habían hallado tan modernos como Desengaño de celos y Ninfas y Pastores de Henares, que también su historia debía de ser moderna; y que, ya que no estuviese escrita, estaría en la memoria de la gente de su aldea y de las a ella circunvecinas.
t: On the other hand, it seemed to me that, since among his books there had been found ones as modern as the Tale of Jealousy and the Nymphs and Shepherds of Henares, his history must also be modern; and that, since it was not written down, it must be in the memory of the people of his village and of the neighboring villages around it.

o: Pasó, pues, el hallarla en esta manera.
t: It came about, then, that I found it in this manner.

o: Estando yo un día en el Alcaná de Toledo, llegó un muchacho a vender unos cartapacios y papeles viejos a un sedero; y, como yo soy aficionado a leer, aunque sean los papeles rotos de las calles, llevado desta mi natural inclinación, tomé un cartapacio de los que el muchacho vendía, y vile con caracteres que conocí ser arábigos.
t: Being one day in the Alcaná of Toledo, a boy came to sell some old scrapbooks and papers to a silk merchant; and since I am fond of reading, even if the papers are torn and picked up from the streets, moved by this natural inclination of mine, I took one of the scrapbooks the boy was selling and saw that it was written in characters I recognized as Arabic.

o: Y, puesto que, aunque los conocía, no los sabía leer, anduve mirando si parecía por allí algún morisco aljamiado que los leyese; y no fue muy dificultoso hallar intérprete semejante, pues, aunque le buscara de otra mejor y más antigua lengua, le hallara.
t: And since, although I knew them, I could not read them, I went looking to see if there seemed to be any Morisco around who could read them in Spanish script; and it was not very difficult to find such an interpreter, for, even if I had sought one from some better and more ancient language, I would have found him.

o: En fin, la suerte me deparó uno, que, diciéndole mi deseo y poniéndole el libro en las manos, le abrió por medio, y, leyendo un poco en él, se comenzó a reír.
t: In short, fortune provided me with one, and, telling him my desire and placing the book in his hands, he opened it in the middle and, reading a little of it, began to laugh.

o: Preguntéle yo que de qué se reía, y respondióme que de una cosa que tenía aquel libro escrita en el margen por anotación.
t: I asked him what he was laughing at, and he answered me that it was at something that book had written in the margin as an annotation.

o: Díjele que me la dijese; y él, sin dejar la risa, dijo.
t: I told him to tell it to me; and he, without stopping laughing, said:

o: — Está, como he dicho, aquí en el margen escrito esto: "Esta Dulcinea del Toboso, tantas veces en esta historia referida, dicen que tuvo la mejor mano para salar puercos que otra mujer de toda la Mancha".
t: "It is, as I have said, written here in the margin: 'This Dulcinea del Toboso, so many times referred to in this history, is said to have had the best hand for salting pigs of any woman in all La Mancha.'"

o: Cuando yo oí decir "Dulcinea del Toboso", quedé atónito y suspenso, porque luego se me representó que aquellos cartapacios contenían la historia de don Quijote.
t: When I heard say "Dulcinea del Toboso," I was astounded and suspended, for immediately it occurred to me that those scrapbooks contained the story of Don Quixote.

o: Con esta imaginación, le di priesa que leyese el principio, y, haciéndolo ansí, volviendo de improviso el arábigo en castellano, dijo que decía: Historia de don Quijote de la Mancha, escrita por Cide Hamete Benengeli, historiador arábigo.
t: With this imagination, I urged him to read the beginning, and, doing so, turning the Arabic back into Castilian on the spur of the moment, he said that it said: Story of Don Quixote of La Mancha, written by Cide Hamete Benengeli, Arab historian.

o: Mucha discreción fue menester para disimular el contento que recebí cuando llegó a mis oídos el título del libro; y, salteándosele al sedero, compré al muchacho todos los papeles y cartapacios por medio real; que, si él tuviera discreción y supiera lo que yo los deseaba, bien se pudiera prometer y llevar más de seis reales de la compra.
t: Much discretion was needed to conceal the joy I felt when the title of the book reached my ears; and, slipping it away from the silk merchant, I bought all the papers and scrapbooks from the boy for half a real; for, if he had had any discretion and had known how much I desired them, he could well have expected and gotten more than six reales for the purchase.

o: Apartéme luego con el morisco por el claustro de la iglesia mayor, y roguéle me volviese aquellos cartapacios, todos los que trataban de don Quijote, en lengua castellana, sin quitarles ni añadirles nada, ofreciéndole la paga que él quisiese.
t: So I drew him aside with the Moor through the cloister of the main church and asked him to give me back those manuscripts — all those that treated of Don Quixote — in the Castilian tongue, without taking anything from them or adding anything to them, offering him whatever payment he might wish.

o: Contentóse con dos arrobas de pasas y dos fanegas de trigo, y prometió de traducirlos bien y fielmente y con mucha brevedad.
t: He was satisfied with two arrobas of raisins and two fanegas of wheat, and promised to translate them well and faithfully and with great brevity.

o: Pero yo, por facilitar más el negocio y por no dejar de la mano tan buen hallazgo, le truje a mi casa, donde en poco más de mes y medio la tradujo toda, del mesmo modo que aquí se refiere.
t: But I, in order to make the business easier and not to let such a good find slip out of my hands, brought him to my house, where in a little over a month and a half he translated the whole of it, in the very manner in which it is set down here.

o: Estaba en el primero cartapacio, pintada muy al natural, la batalla de don Quijote con el vizcaíno, puestos en la mesma postura que la historia cuenta, levantadas las espadas, el uno cubierto de su rodela, el otro de la almohada, y la mula del vizcaíno tan al vivo, que estaba mostrando ser de alquiler a tiro de ballesta.
t: In the first manuscript the battle of Don Quixote with the Biscayan was painted very lifelike, the two of them set in the very posture the history describes, with their swords raised, the one covered by his shield, the other by his cushion, and the Biscayan's mule so vividly portrayed that it seemed to be a mount for hire, good for a bolt's flight.

o: Tenía a los pies escrito el vizcaíno un título que decía: Don Sancho de Azpetia, que, sin duda, debía de ser su nombre, y a los pies de Rocinante estaba otro que decía: Don Quijote.
t: At the Biscayan's feet there was written a title which said: Don Sancho de Azpetia, which was undoubtedly his name, and at Rocinante's feet another which said: Don Quijote.

o: Estaba Rocinante maravillosamente pintado, tan largo y tendido, tan atenuado y flaco, con tanto espinazo, tan hético confirmado, que mostraba bien al descubierto con cuánta advertencia y propriedad se le había puesto el nombre de Rocinante.
t: Rocinante was wonderfully painted, so long and lanky, so attenuated and thin, with so much backbone, so confirmedly scraggy, that it showed plainly, and beyond all doubt, with what care and good judgment the name of Rocinante had been bestowed upon him.

o: Otras algunas menudencias había que advertir, pero todas son de poca importancia y que no hacen al caso a la verdadera relación de la historia; que ninguna es mala como sea verdadera.
t: There were certain other trifles to be noted, but they are all of little importance and do not bear upon the true relation of the history; and none of them is bad so long as it is true.

o: Si a ésta se le puede poner alguna objeción cerca de su verdad, no podrá ser otra sino haber sido su autor arábigo, siendo muy propio de los de aquella nación ser mentirosos; aunque, por ser tan nuestros enemigos, antes se puede entender haber quedado falto en ella que demasiado.
t: If any objection can be raised against this one as to its truth, it can only be that its author was an Arab, it being very much the way of those of that nation to be liars; though, since they are such enemies of ours, it may rather be understood that it fell short in truth than that it said too much.

o: En ésta sé que se hallará todo lo que se acertare a desear en la más apacible; y si algo bueno en ella faltare, para mí tengo que fue por culpa del galgo de su autor, antes que por falta del sujeto.
t: In this one I know that everything that could possibly be desired will be found in the most peaceful terms; and if anything good were lacking in it, for me the fault lies with the author's greyhound rather than with the subject.

o: En fin, su segunda parte, siguiendo la tradución, comenzaba desta manera.
t: In short, its second part, following the translation, began in this manner.

o: Puestas y levantadas en alto las cortadoras espadas de los dos valerosos y enojados combatientes, no parecía sino que estaban amenazando al cielo, a la tierra y al abismo: tal era el denuedo y continente que tenían.
t: With the sharp swords of the two valiant and angry combatants raised high on high, it seemed as though they were threatening heaven, earth, and the abyss: such was the boldness and self-possession that they had.

o: ¡Válame Dios, y quién será aquel que buenamente pueda contar ahora la rabia que entró en el corazón de nuestro manchego, viéndose parar de aquella manera!
t: God help me, and who is there who could now tell in full the rage that entered the heart of our Manchegan, beholding himself stopped in that manner!

o: Estábaselo con mucho sosiego mirando don Quijote, y, como lo vio caer, saltó de su caballo y con mucha ligereza se llegó a él, y, poniéndole la punta de la espada en los ojos, le dijo que se rindiese; si no, que le cortaría la cabeza.
t: Don Quixote was gazing at him with great composure, and as he saw him fall, he sprang from his horse and with great lightness came up to him, and, setting the point of his sword against his eyes, told him to yield; if not, he would cut off his head.

o: Estaba el vizcaíno tan turbado que no podía responder palabra, y él lo pasara mal, según estaba ciego don Quijote, si las señoras del coche, que hasta entonces con gran desmayo habían mirado la pendencia, no fueran adonde estaba y le pidieran con mucho encarecimiento les hiciese tan gran merced y favor de perdonar la vida a aquel su escudero.
t: The Biscayan was so confused that he could not answer a word, and he would have fared badly, since Don Quixote was blinded with rage, if the ladies of the coach, who until then had watched the affray with great dismay, had not come up to where he was and entreated him with much insistence that he would grant them the great mercy and favor of sparing the life of their squire.

o: A lo cual don Quijote respondió, con mucho entono y gravedad.
t: To which Don Quixote replied with much stateliness and gravity.

o: — Por cierto, fermosas señoras, yo soy muy contento de hacer lo que me pedís; mas ha de ser con una condición y concierto, y es que este caballero me ha de prometer de ir al lugar del Toboso y presentarse de mi parte ante la sin par doña Dulcinea, para que ella haga dél lo que más fuere de su voluntad.
t: — Indeed, fair ladies, I am very glad to do what you ask of me; but it must be on one condition and agreement, and that is, that this knight must promise me to go to the place of Toboso and present himself on my behalf before the peerless Doña Dulcinea, so that she may do with him whatever she shall most desire.

o: La temerosa y desconsolada señora, sin entrar en cuenta de lo que don Quijote pedía, y sin preguntar quién Dulcinea fuese, le prometió que el escudero haría todo aquello que de su parte le fuese mandado.
t: The timid and disconsolate lady, without taking into account what Don Quixote was asking, and without asking who Dulcinea was, promised him that the squire would do everything that should be commanded of him on her behalf.

o: — Pues en fe de esa palabra, yo no le haré más daño, puesto que me lo tenía bien merecido.
t: — Well then, on the pledge of that word, I will do him no further harm, since he had well deserved it.

o: Capítulo X. De lo que más le avino a don Quijote con el vizcaíno, y del peligro en que se vio con una turba de yangüeses.
t: Chapter X. Of what befell Don Quixote with the Biscayan, and of the danger in which he found himself with a mob of Yanguesans.

o: Ya en este tiempo se había levantado Sancho Panza, algo maltratado de los mozos de los frailes, y había estado atento a la batalla de su señor don Quijote, y rogaba a Dios en su corazón fuese servido de darle vitoria y que en ella ganase alguna ínsula de donde le hiciese gobernador, como se lo había prometido.
t: By this time Sancho Panza had risen, somewhat roughed up by the friars' boys, and had been watching attentively the battle of his master Don Quixote, and he prayed to God in his heart that he would be served to grant him the victory, and that in it he might win some island where he would make him governor, as he had promised him.

o: Viendo, pues, ya acabada la pendencia, y que su amo volvía a subir sobre Rocinante, llegó a tenerle el estribo; y antes que subiese se hincó de rodillas delante dél, y, asiéndole de la mano, se la besó y le dijo.
t: Seeing, then, that the affair was over and that his master was mounting Rocinante again, he came to hold the stirrup for him; and before he mounted, he knelt down before him and, taking him by the hand, kissed it and said to him.

o: — Sea vuestra merced servido, señor don Quijote mío, de darme el gobierno de la ínsula que en esta rigurosa pendencia se ha ganado; que, por grande que sea, yo me siento con fuerzas de saberla gobernar tal y tan bien como otro que haya gobernado ínsulas en el mundo.
t: "May your worship, sir, my own master Don Quixote, be pleased to grant me the government of the island that I have won in this bitter business; for however great it may be, I feel strong enough to know how to govern it as well and as ably as any other who has governed islands in the world."

o: A lo cual respondió don Quijote.
t: To which Don Quixote replied.

o: — Advertid, hermano Sancho, que esta aventura y las a ésta semejantes no son aventuras de ínsulas, sino de encrucijadas, en las cuales no se gana otra cosa que sacar rota la cabeza o una oreja menos.
t: "Be warned, brother Sancho, that this adventure and those like it are not adventures of islands, but of crossroads, where all one wins is a broken head or a missing ear."

o: Tened paciencia, que aventuras se ofrecerán donde no solamente os pueda hacer gobernador, sino más adelante.
t: Be patient, for adventures will present themselves where you may not only become governor, but go further still.

o: Agradecióselo mucho Sancho, y, besándole otra vez la mano y la falda de la loriga, le ayudó a subir sobre Rocinante; y él subió sobre su asno y comenzó a seguir a su señor, que, a paso tirado, sin despedirse ni hablar más con las del coche, se entró por un bosque que allí junto estaba.
t: Sancho thanked him greatly, and, kissing his hand and the skirt of his armor once more, helped him mount Rocinante; and he climbed onto his donkey and began to follow his master, who, at a brisk pace, without taking leave of or speaking further with those in the coach, rode off into a wood that lay close by.

o: Seguíale Sancho a todo el trote de su jumento, pero caminaba tanto Rocinante que, viéndose quedar atrás, le fue forzoso dar voces a su amo que se aguardase.
t: Sancho followed at the full trot of his beast, but Rocinante went so fast that, finding himself left behind, he was forced to call out to his master to wait for him.

o: Hízolo así don Quijote, teniendo las riendas a Rocinante hasta que llegase su cansado escudero, el cual, en llegando, le dijo.
t: Don Quixote did so, holding the reins of Rocinante until his weary squire arrived, who, on coming up, said to him:

o: — Paréceme, señor, que sería acertado irnos a retraer a alguna iglesia; que, según quedó maltrecho aquel con quien os combatistes, no será mucho que den noticia del caso a la Santa Hermandad y nos prendan; y a fe que si lo hacen, que primero que salgamos de la cárcel que nos ha de sudar el hopo.
t: "It seems to me, sir, that it would be wise for us to withdraw to some church; for, judging by how badly he fared, the one you fought with, it will not be long before the Holy Brotherhood hears of the matter and arrests us; and on my word, if they do, we shall be in the clink before we get out of the jail that is going to cost us our hide."

o: — Calla —dijo don Quijote—.
t: "Be quiet," said Don Quixote.

o: Y ¿dónde has visto tú, o leído jamás, que caballero andante haya sido puesto ante la justicia, por más homicidios que hubiese cometido?
t: And where have you ever seen or read, that a knight-errant was ever handed over to the authorities, however many homicides he had committed?

o: — Yo no sé nada de omecillos —respondió Sancho—, ni en mi vida le caté a ninguno; sólo sé que la Santa Hermandad tiene que ver con los que pelean en el campo, y en esotro no me entremeto.
t: "I know nothing about such trifles," replied Sancho, "nor have I ever meddled with any of them; I only know that the Holy Brotherhood has to do with those who fight in the open field, and into that business I do not meddle."

o: — Pues no tengas pena, amigo —respondió don Quijote—, que yo te sacaré de las manos de los caldeos, cuanto más de las de la Hermandad.
t: "Then do not worry, friend," replied Don Quixote, "for I shall rescue you from the hands of the Chaldeans, let alone from those of the Brotherhood."

o: Pero dime, por tu vida: ¿has visto más valeroso caballero que yo en todo lo descubierto de la tierra?
t: But tell me, on your life: have you ever seen a more valorous knight than me, in all the world discovered so far?

o: ¿Has leído en historias otro que tenga ni haya tenido más brío en acometer, más aliento en el perseverar, más destreza en el herir, ni más maña en el derribar?
t: Have you read in any history of another who has had, or ever had, more boldness in attacking, more endurance in persevering, more skill in wounding, or more cunning in felling his foe?

o: — La verdad sea —respondió Sancho— que yo no he leído ninguna historia jamás, porque ni sé leer ni escrebir; mas lo que osaré apostar es que más atrevido amo que vuestra merced yo no le he servido en todos los días de mi vida, y quiera Dios que estos atrevimientos no se paguen donde tengo dicho.
t: "The truth be told," replied Sancho, "I have never read a single history, because I neither know how to read nor how to write; but what I dare wager is that I have never served a bolder master than your worship in all the days of my life, and God grant that these boldnesses do not be paid for where I have said."

o: Lo que le ruego a vuestra merced es que se cure, que le va mucha sangre de esa oreja; que aquí traigo hilas y un poco de ungüento blanco en las alforjas.
t: What I ask of your worship is that you be treated, for you are losing a lot of blood from that ear; here I have lint and a little white ointment in my saddlebags.

o: — Todo eso fuera bien escusado —respondió don Quijote— si a mí se me acordara de hacer una redoma del bálsamo de Fierabrás, que con sola una gota se ahorraran tiempo y medicinas.
t: "All that would be needless," replied Don Quixote, "if I could remember to make a vial of Fierabras's balsam, with which a single drop would spare both time and medicine."

o: — ¿Qué redoma y qué bálsamo es ése?
t: "What vial and what balsam is that?"

o: —dijo Sancho Panza.
t: "—said Sancho Panza."

o: — Es un bálsamo —respondió don Quijote— de quien tengo la receta en la memoria, con el cual no hay que tener temor a la muerte, ni hay pensar morir de ferida alguna.
t: "It is a balsam," replied Don Quixote, "of a kind whose recipe I have by heart, with which one need not fear death, nor need one think of dying of any wound."

o: — Si eso hay —dijo Panza—, yo renuncio desde aquí el gobierno de la prometida ínsula, y no quiero otra cosa, en pago de mis muchos y buenos servicios, sino que vuestra merced me dé la receta de ese estremado licor; que para mí tengo que valdrá la onza adondequiera más de a dos reales, y no he menester yo más para pasar esta vida honrada y descansadamente.
t: "If that is so," said Panza, "I hereby renounce the government of the promised island, and I want nothing else, in payment for my many and good services, but that your grace give me the recipe for that excellent cordial; for to me it must be worth an ounce anywhere for more than two reales, and I need nothing more to live an honest and comfortable life."

o: Pero es de saber agora si tiene mucha costa el hacelle.
t: But it is to be known now whether it costs much to make it.

o: — Con menos de tres reales se pueden hacer tres azumbres —respondió don Quijote.
t: "With less than three reales one can make three azumbres," replied Don Quixote.

o: —replicó Sancho—.
t: "replied Sancho."

o: ¿Pues a qué aguarda vuestra merced a hacelle y a enseñármele?
t: "Then why does your grace wait to make it and show it to me?"

o: — Calla, amigo —respondió don Quijote—, que mayores secretos pienso enseñarte y mayores mercedes hacerte; y, por agora, curémonos, que la oreja me duele más de lo que yo quisiera.
t: "Be quiet, friend," replied Don Quixote, "for I mean to teach you greater secrets and do you greater favors; and for now, let us cure this, for my ear hurts me more than I would wish."

o: Sacó Sancho de las alforjas hilas y ungüento.
t: Sancho took lint and ointment from his saddlebags.

o: Mas, cuando don Quijote llegó a ver rota su celada, pensó perder el juicio, y, puesta la mano en la espada y alzando los ojos al cielo, dijo.
t: But when Don Quixote came to see his helmet in pieces, he thought he would lose his mind, and, setting his hand on his sword and lifting his eyes to heaven, he said.

o: Oyendo esto Sancho, le dijo.
t: Hearing this, Sancho said to him.

o: — Advierta vuestra merced, señor don Quijote, que si el caballero cumplió lo que se le dejó ordenado de irse a presentar ante mi señora Dulcinea del Toboso, ya habrá cumplido con lo que debía, y no merece otra pena si no comete nuevo delito.
t: "Let your grace take notice, sir Don Quixote, that if the knight did what he was ordered to do, namely, go and present himself before my lady Dulcinea del Toboso, he has already done what he had to do, and he deserves no further punishment unless he commits a new offense."

o: — Has hablado y apuntado muy bien —respondió don Quijote—; y así, anulo el juramento en cuanto lo que toca a tomar dél nueva venganza; pero hágole y confírmole de nuevo de hacer la vida que he dicho, hasta tanto que quite por fuerza otra celada tal y tan buena como ésta a algún caballero.
t: "You have spoken and hit the mark very well," replied Don Quixote; "and so, I annul the oath insofar as it concerns taking fresh vengeance upon him; but I make it and confirm it anew that I will pursue the life I have described, until I wrest by force from some knight another ambush as good and as fine as this one."

o: Y no pienses, Sancho, que así a humo de pajas hago esto, que bien tengo a quien imitar en ello; que esto mesmo pasó, al pie de la letra, sobre el yelmo de Mambrino, que tan caro le costó a Sacripante.
t: And do not think, Sancho, that I do this on a whim, for I have good precedent for it; the very same thing happened, word for word, over Mambrino's helmet, which cost Sacripante so dearly.

o: — Que dé al diablo vuestra merced tales juramentos, señor mío —replicó Sancho—; que son muy en daño de la salud y muy en perjuicio de la conciencia.
t: "May your worship go to the devil with such oaths, my lord," Sancho replied; "they are very bad for the health and very harmful to the conscience."

o: Si no, dígame ahora: si acaso en muchos días no topamos hombre armado con celada, ¿qué hemos de hacer?
t: If not, tell me now: if in many days' time we do not come across an armed man wearing a helmet, what are we to do?

o: ¿Hase de cumplir el juramento, a despecho de tantos inconvenientes e incomodidades, como será el dormir vestido, y el no dormir en poblado, y otras mil penitencias que contenía el juramento de aquel loco viejo del marqués de Mantua, que vuestra merced quiere revalidar ahora?
t: Is the oath to be kept, in spite of all such inconveniences and hardships as sleeping in one's clothes, not sleeping in a town, and the thousand other penances contained in the oath of that mad old man, the Marquis of Mantua, which your worship now wants to renew?

o: Mire vuestra merced bien, que por todos estos caminos no andan hombres armados, sino arrieros y carreteros, que no sólo no traen celadas, pero quizá no las han oído nombrar en todos los días de su vida.
t: Let your worship look well: along all these roads there are no armed men, only muleteers and carters, who not only never wear helmets but have perhaps never even heard the word.

o: — Engáñaste en eso —dijo don Quijote—, porque no habremos estado dos horas por estas encrucijadas, cuando veamos más armados que los que vinieron sobre Albraca a la conquista de Angélica la Bella.
t: "You are mistaken there," said Don Quixote, "for we shall not have been two hours on these crossroads before we see more armed men than those who came upon Albraca to conquer the fair Angélica."

o: — Alto, pues; sea ansí —dijo Sancho—, y a Dios prazga que nos suceda bien, y que se llegue ya el tiempo de ganar esta ínsula que tan cara me cuesta, y muérame yo luego.
t: "Very well, then; so be it," said Sancho; "and may God grant that all goes well with us, and that the time has come for us to win this island, which is costing me so dearly, and may I die on the spot."

o: — Ya te he dicho, Sancho, que no te dé eso cuidado alguno; que, cuando faltare ínsula, ahí está el reino de Dinamarca o el de Soliadisa, que te vendrán como anillo al dedo; y más, que, por ser en tierra firme, te debes más alegrar.
t: "I have already told you, Sancho, that you need not worry about that at all; for if there is no island left, there is the kingdom of Denmark or that of Soliadisa, which will fit you like a glove; and besides, since they are on the mainland, you have more reason to be glad."

o: Pero dejemos esto para su tiempo, y mira si traes algo en esas alforjas que comamos, porque vamos luego en busca de algún castillo donde alojemos esta noche y hagamos el bálsamo que te he dicho; porque yo te voto a Dios que me va doliendo mucho la oreja.
t: But let us leave that for its time, and see if you have anything in those saddlebags for us to eat, because we are going straight off to look for some castle where we may lodge tonight and make the balsam I told you about; for I swear to God, my ear is hurting me badly.

o: — Aquí trayo una cebolla, y un poco de queso y no sé cuántos mendrugos de pan —dijo Sancho—, pero no son manjares que pertenecen a tan valiente caballero como vuestra merced.
t: "Here I bring an onion, and a bit of cheese, and I don't know how many scraps of bread," said Sancho, "but these are not dishes fit for so valorous a knight as your Grace."

o: — ¡Qué mal lo entiendes!
t: "How badly you understand things!"

o: —respondió don Quijote—.
t: "replied Don Quixote."

o: Así que, Sancho amigo, no te congoje lo que a mí me da gusto.
t: "So, Sancho my friend, don't begrudge me what gives me pleasure."

o: Ni querrás tú hacer mundo nuevo, ni sacar la caballería andante de sus quicios.
t: "Nor would you want to make a new world, nor to knock chivalry from its hinges."

o: — No digo yo, Sancho —replicó don Quijote—, que sea forzoso a los caballeros andantes no comer otra cosa sino esas frutas que dices, sino que su más ordinario sustento debía de ser dellas, y de algunas yerbas que hallaban por los campos, que ellos conocían y yo también conozco.
t: "I do not say, Sancho," replied Don Quixote, "that it is obligatory for knights-errant to eat nothing but the fruits you mention, but that their ordinary sustenance ought to consist of those, and of certain herbs they found in the fields, which they knew and which I know as well."

o: — Virtud es —respondió Sancho— conocer esas yerbas; que, según yo me voy imaginando, algún día será menester usar de ese conocimiento.
t: "It is a virtue," answered Sancho, "to know those herbs; for, as I imagine, some day there will be need to make use of that knowledge."

o: Y, sacando, en esto, lo que dijo que traía, comieron los dos en buena paz y compaña.
t: And, taking out what he had said he was carrying, the two of them ate in good peace and fellowship.

o: Pero, deseosos de buscar donde alojar aquella noche, acabaron con mucha brevedad su pobre y seca comida.
t: But, eager to find where to lodge that night, they finished their meager and dry meal very quickly.
